title: In 8 to 10 Hours, Your Flush Is Clean Water Again #shorts
summary: New York City's 14 plants treat 1.3 billion gallons of wastewater a day: bar screens, settling tanks, air for oxygen-loving microbes, disinfection with sodium hypochlorite, then clean water out after about 8-10 hours (NYC DEP).
sources: NYC treatment: bar screens; primary settling tanks where the flow slows down and heavier sludge settles; air added so oxygen-loving microorganisms consume much of the organic material; final settling; disinfection with sodium hypochlorite, the same chemical found in household bleach; after about 8-10 hours the facilities release clean water; digesters heated to about 98°F for about 15 days, where microorganisms convert much of the material into biogas, which can produce heat and electricity for the facilities (NYC DEP, Wastewater Treatment System): https://www.nyc.gov/site/dep/water/wastewater-treatment-process.page

New York City has 14 Wastewater Resource Recovery Facilities that together treat 1.3 billion gallons of wastewater daily; more than 6,000 miles of sewer pipes; 95 pumping stations (NYC DEP, Wastewater Resource Recovery Facilities): https://www.nyc.gov/site/dep/water/wastewater-treatment-plants.page

Screening removes large floating objects such as rags and sticks that might clog pipes or damage equipment; in a grit chamber cinders, sand and small stones settle; secondary (biological) treatment removes about 85 percent of the organic matter in sewage; done properly, chlorination kills more than 99 percent of the harmful bacteria in an effluent (US EPA, Wastewater Treatment Works... The Basics, EPA 833-F-98-002, May 1998): https://www3.epa.gov/npdes/pubs/bastre.pdf

scenes.narration: In New York, your flush becomes clean water in about {8–10|eight to ten} hours.
First, screens catch rags and sticks.
In settling tanks, the heavy solids sink.
Then air goes in, and microbes eat the organic matter.
A chemical found in bleach disinfects it.
The city does this to {1.3 billion|one point three billion} gallons a day.
Then it's released, clean. So next time you flush:
